title: Which reruns owe you the same bits?

blocks.text: A grid operator keeps a record of every LP and MILP run: its `inputs` (a snapshot id), the `device`, the `solver`, the `method`, the `threads`, the `tolerance`, the `versions`, the `kind` (`"lp"` or `"milp"`), the `objective` and a `digest` of the solution's bits. When a run is repeated, the auditors want a verdict that holds a rerun to its bits only where the configuration promised them, and to a tolerance everywhere else.

Bits are promised when the two runs agree on every one of inputs, device, solver, method, threads, tolerance and versions, **unless** the method is `"concurrent"` (a race whose winner can change) or the run is a cuOpt (`solver == "cuopt"`) MILP, whose plans did not repeat with any setting.

items: `bits_promised(a, b)`: True when the rule above promises equal bits;

`verdict(a, b, tol)`: `"not comparable"` when the inputs differ; where bits are promised, `"identical"` when digest and objective are equal and `"different"` otherwise; else `"within tolerance"` when the objectives differ by at most `tol` relatively (divided by $`\max(1, \lvert a\text{'s objective} \rvert)`$), and `"different"` otherwise.

blocks.text: The tests pass run records; no solver runs. About fifteen lines.

    run = {"inputs": "lp-7", "device": "cpu", "solver": "highs", "method": "simplex", "threads": 1, "tolerance": 1e-7,

cases.says: a rerun of one configuration that repeats is held to its bits
runs on different devices are compared within the tolerance, and other inputs are not compared
a concurrent run is not held to its bits
a cuOpt MILP run is not held to its bits
a different thread count is another configuration
the tolerance is relative to the objective

origin.section: cuOpt's MILP Did Not Repeat, Even in Its Determinism Mode

concepts: bits are owed only by a rerun of one configuration that repeats; races, cuOpt MILPs and other thread counts are held to a tolerance
